name: Dzhankoi-Henichesk Gas Pipeline (Crimea to Kherson Oblast reverse-flow line)
monitor_reason: length: no sourced length anywhere. Also sponsor unclear (Gazprom-prepared design, Chernomorneftegaz as builder is not stated for this line) and the work is a reverse-flow reconstruction of the old Soviet Kherson-Crimea trunk, so it may add no new pipe.
researcher_notes: Not an existing GEM row: P1457, P5989, P7817 and P7818 are Taganrog-Mariupol/Melitopol-Berdyansk lines, and no existing row covers Dzhankoi or Henichesk. Checked three Russian-language articles that load and name the line. RIA, 16 March 2023: Saldo says construction of a gas line from Crimea to the Henichesk area has begun, fed from the old trunk that once ran from Kherson Oblast to Crimea and now runs in reverse. RIA Crimea, 26 October 2023: the Crimea to Kherson Oblast trunk was rebuilt, so this reuses existing pipe, which answers the reuse question: it is a reconstruction and reverse of the old Kherson-Crimea trunk, with a branch toward Henichesk. VZ, 27 August 2025: Saldo says a reverse branch from Crimea cost 1.7 billion rubles. No source gives length, diameter, capacity or the exact route. The occupying administration and Russian state companies are the builders, reported as builders only. Left as monitor. If a sourced length of 25 km or more appears, or the new-pipe part is shown, it could be added as a Ukraine row. The three sources are all Russian state-linked media, so not fully independent.
